items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 22 at 4:42PM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Crystal Coast beaches.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
items.instruction:
Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued September 22 at 2:33PM EDT until September 25 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and
seas 6 to 15 ft expected.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Surf City,
and the offshore waters from Cape Lookout to Surf City.

* WHEN...From 2 PM Wednesday to midnight EDT Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong coastal low will develop offshore
east of North Carolina by Wednesday, then move north towards the
coast of New England by the end of the week. This low is
expected to produce an extended period of hazardous marine
conditions for much of the ENC waters.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
